definition: Core knowledge is the central know-how or information a team relies on in its work. In competitive collaborative settings, it may be kept confidential, which can restrict knowledge sharing and make open collaboration harder.

reasons: The packet does not define “core knowledge” as “the central know-how or information a team relies on”; it only mentions that the competitive nature of design teams often “keeps core knowledge confidential.”

The claim that confidentiality “can restrict knowledge sharing and make open collaboration harder” is only indirectly supported (the packet says confidentiality hinders collaboration), but the first sentence is unsupported, so the overall definition cannot be accepted.
The packet supports a design-collaboration meaning of “core knowledge” as confidential knowledge in competitive teams, not the broader gloss “the central know-how or information a team relies on.”
